source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Obsessive-compulsive disorder, when obsessions and compulsions are present but are not centered on perceived appearance defects.","B":"Social anxiety disorder, when fear of scrutiny or embarrassment is primary without a persistent perceived appearance flaw.","C":"Illness anxiety disorder, when fear of having or acquiring serious disease is primary rather than perceived appearance defects.","D":"Body dysmorphic disorder, characterized by preoccupation with slight or unobservable appearance flaws plus repetitive appearance-related behaviors."}}
source_row.rationale: Body dysmorphic disorder involves preoccupation with perceived defects that are not observable or appear slight to others, repetitive appearance-related behaviors such as mirror checking/reassurance seeking, and clinically significant distress or impairment.

source_row.stem: A client is preoccupied with a slight or unnoticeable perceived flaw in appearance, repeatedly checks mirrors and seeks reassurance, and has substantial social impairment. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
